newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuelan bolivar ends off despite TEM rate rise.
newsitem.headline: Venezuelan bolivar ends off despite TEM rate rise.

text.p: The Venezuelan bolivar softened to 474.54/475.75 bolivars per dollar in active trade despite Central Bank intervention and a 158-basis-point rise in the benchmark TEM bill rate, traders said.
Despite the rate rise, traders said Venezuelan rates were still relatively low.
"While they (rates) remain low, demand for dollars is going to continue," said one trader.
On Tuesday, the unit closed at 474.25/475.25 per dollar.
"Companies are increasingly moving into dollars to protect themselves from any eventual exchange rate adjustment," he added.

Some traders fear a sharp devaluation in what most agree is an overvalued bolivar. But most expect the Central Bank to continue its gradual weakening of the currency, breaking the bolivar's fall by gently feeding the market dollars.
